Subject: Availability rider + evidence routing for MSA/order form

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — Healix is moving fast and procurement asked me to consolidate the asks so legal can review. Two items they want in an Exhibit attached to the order form:

1) An availability rider that documents regional availability tiers and the proposed service credit schedule for degraded mode. We don't need a 99.99% carveout, but we do need firm guidance on how credits are calculated for sustained latency regressions.

2) A list of operational evidence we can request during onboarding and for periodic audits (SOC2 scans, regional failover test reports, token-level latency histograms for 30-day windows). Procurement asked for a one-page index they can attach to the SOW.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with the fields they want populated (column names only). Can you confirm: (a) whether Redwood can accept the rider language as-is or propose alternate order form language, and (b) where Healix should expect to request the evidence (contact, flow, SLA ticketing)?

We're hoping to close procurement review this week — legal will need the draft exhibit to start redlines.

Appreciate it,

Samantha Ortiz

Subject: Redwood: draft availability rider + proposed order-form wording

Samantha / team — attached is a working draft of the availability rider and a short order-form exhibit (Redwood-proposed-availability-rider_v2.docx). Highlights:

- Regional tiers: US-EAST (primary), US-WEST (redundant), EU (optional). Each region has a defined target availability over 30-day windows.
- Credit formula: credits calculated as percentage of monthly service fees per impacted region, prorated by affected customer endpoints and by duration of breach measured in contiguous 1-hour windows after detection. We used a 4-step degradation table (Latency Preservation, Moderate Degradation, Severe Degradation, Outage).
- Degraded-mode fallback: automatic routing to a cost-tier model variant with documented fidelity loss and a stated max QPS.

I've purposely kept the credit math transparent (example calculation included) so your procurement folks can map to their internal finance models.

Evidence routing proposal (summary):
- Initial request via procurement@redwood (or HubSpot request linked to the deal).
- We provide an evidence packet (index + documents) within 10 business days for standard items (SOC2, encryption certs, uptime reports).
- For deep forensic requests (KV cache traces, token-level histograms), we propose a 20-business-day window and an ops-led review call.

Attachments: Redwood-proposed-availability-rider_v2.docx (order-form exhibit) and a template evidence-index we can populate.

Next steps: if Healix legal redlines, please send to k_iyer@redwood.ai (cc'd if necessary) and we'll triage. Samantha — would you like us to put the draft into DocuSign so your legal team can markup inline?

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer

Samantha — quick ops perspective and suggested runbook for evidence requests so procurement has clear expectations:

1) Evidence index (one-pager):
  - SOC2 Type II report (last 12 months) — PDF stub
  - Regional failover test summary (date, scope, outcome) — PDF/slide
  - 30-day latency histogram per token class (aggregated, P95/P99) — CSV (redacted PII)
  - Incident timeline (for any requested outage) — Ops memo (DOCX)

2) Request flow:
  - Procurement sends request to procurement@redwood.ai with Deal ID in subject.
  - Auto-ticket created in our vendor-evidence queue; procurement gets an acknowledgement email within 24 hours.
  - Standard evidence items delivered as a zipped packet within 10 business days. Deep forensics require a signed non-disclosure addendum and a joint scoping call; target delivery 20 business days after scoping.

3) Contact points:
  - Evidence coordinator: monica_patel@redwood.ai (procurement liaison)
  - Ops lead for forensics: ops-oncall@redwood.ai

I'll prepare the evidence-index.zip (placeholder) and share a Drive link once it's populated. Also flagging that token-level histograms are aggregated and redacted; we won't provide raw logs or KV-contents without an executed forensics engagement.

— Monica Patel

Samantha, Priyom — we reviewed the draft rider and evidence flow. A few legal notes before we finalize for DocuSign:

1) Credit definition: please confirm you accept the contiguous 1-hour window incrementing approach (we used it to prevent micro-flapping from producing credits). If Healix requires a different granularity, call it out and we'll adapt math.

2) For the evidence index, we will provide the standard SOC2 and failover summaries without redaction requests. Any request for raw token-level logs or KV cache inspection requires a scoped forensics SOW (we included a one-paragraph placeholder in the exhibit). That SOW will include rates and delivery timelines.

3) Export control / regional data: the rider currently references regional availability but does not change data residency commitments — if Healix requires hard residency guarantees we will need to elevate to Solutions Architecture and estimate a dedicated deployment.

If Healix legal can accept the draft with the above anchors, we can convert the document to a tracked-change DocuSign envelope for inline redlines. Otherwise, send back marked PDF comments and we'll triage.

I'll stand by for the redlines and will join any review call.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
